title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: JFrog
providers.scope_notes: Covers JFrog Platform (Cloud/SaaS). JFrog Cloud SaaS; IP allowlist, OIDC integration and MyJFrog API tokens need Enterprise X or Enterprise+, log streaming needs Enterprise+, Cloud Log Collection is on all SaaS licenses; several token thresholds are documented only as self-hosted YAML settings.

controls.name: Disable API Key Usage
controls.what: Blocks authentication with existing API keys.
controls.setting: Administration > Security > General > Disable API Key Usage

controls.name: IP/CIDR Allowlist
controls.what: Only listed IPs/JPDs can reach the JPD.
controls.setting: MyJFrog > Security > Allowlist; MyJFrog IP allowlist API

controls.name: Allow Created Users Access To Profile Page
controls.what: When cleared, users auto-created through SAML cannot reach their profile page, where identity tokens and API keys are generated.
controls.setting: Administration > Authentication Providers > SAML SSO settings

no_control.what: Admins cannot monitor or manage individual users' API keys (only the global disable and a user list).

controls_unknown: Whether SaaS customers can change token.max-expiry, token.allow-refreshable or revocable-expiry-threshold (documented only as Access YAML settings).
A setting to stop non-admin users creating identity tokens.
Default and maximum lifetime of UI-generated identity tokens.
Whether the IP allowlist covers the MyJFrog portal API.
Whether MyJFrog audit logs record API token generation (event names not listed).
Reference token length: Access Tokens page says 128 characters, Identity Tokens page says 64.

authentication.summary: Per-user static key sent in the X-JFrog-Art-Api header or as the basic-auth password. Creation is disabled since Artifactory 7.98, but existing keys keep working unless an admin turns on 'Disable API Key Usage'.

federation.details: Docs do not address SSO interaction for API keys.

renewal.summary: Static until revoked; migrate to reference tokens.

administration.summary: Admin can block all API key use with one checkbox (Security > General > Disable API Key Usage, off by default) and download a CSV of users still using API keys.

inventory.details: Cloud admins can download a CSV of users still using API keys, but cannot otherwise monitor or manage users' keys.

inventory.ui: Administration > User Management > Users > banner download link (CSV of users using API keys)

reads.ui: Administration > Artifactory > System Logs (access log): filter [ACCEPTED DOWNLOAD] with auth type APIKEY

kill.ui: Administration > Security > General > Disable API Key Usage

credential_id_fields.notes: Per-user only; one key per user.

containment.steps: Enable Disable API Key Usage; revoke the user's key.
containment.notes: Checkbox blocks API key usage platform-wide.

calls.log_notes: Request log; access log shows APIKEY type for logins.
Artifactory access log records downloads with user name, IP and auth type APIKEY.
